The whole repertoire on one map, and every connection on it

The book sits in the middle. Each ring out from it is one AIM level: the eight categories, then their groups, then the part types. The outer ring is the 22 distributors. A ribbon between a part type and a distributor means that market actually bills that part type, and the ribbon is as thick as the euro. Parts billed 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2026. Opens from Explorer with no server and no internet.

How the four rings divide the book

Read top to bottom: the categories, then the largest groups, then the largest part types, then the markets. Each row is a share of the same €34,993,609, so the numbers are comparable down the table.
What the middle of the map is, and what it is not. The centre is the €34,993,609 of parts billed in this window — the slice of the repertoire that actually moved money. The AIM tree classifies part numbers; only of them billed here, so classified part numbers are not on this map at all. They carry no quantity, no euro and no price move, and a count of parts with no revenue is not a finding. The map shows what moved, and names the gap rather than drawing the silent 90% as if it were business.
How to read it, and the limits.
  • A wedge is as wide as its share of parts billed euro. The geometry never moves when you change the colour, so the map stays comparable while you look at different measures.
  • The weighted percentage is a base-price move on the quantity-weighted prior base price. It is not a revenue, margin or elasticity outcome, and no demand response is modelled.
  • Ribbons are drawn from a part type to the markets that bill it. A market with no ribbon on a leaf genuinely does not bill that part type — that is a real zero, not a missing figure.
  • A part number with no catalogue node is labelled UNCLASSIFIED and carried, so the category arcs add up to the shipped revision total.
  • The commercial score — contested or captive, per part per market — is a separate axis and is not built as columns yet, so this map cannot show it. It does not guess from the Isuzu figure key.
  • Israel is UMI and UTI separately, never blended. Source of supply (Japan through IML against Thailand through IMIT) is not on this map yet.
